summary: Retest of mobile auth-timing fix from iteration_124 — PASS on all auth-gated flows. Verified: (1) chat-knowledge-chip renders 'AI knows 3 ZIPs' on cold load of /chat/d77a7d2a; (2) tapping the chip navigates to /documents; (3) direct URL /documents (cold) lists all 5 sources (Semantic KB, Chat KB, 2x chatzip.zip, test.zip); (4) opening a Ready source and asking a question end-to-end works for BOTH Claude Sonnet 4.6 AND GPT-5.5 — documents-answer + documents-citations render correctly with real content from notes.txt/team.csv/report.md; (5) documents-upload-btn from /documents flow works — uploaded /tmp/test_facts.zip, ingested to Ready (3 files, 3 chunks) automatically. NEW BUG FOUND (unrelated to the retest, but critical for the zip-in-chat scenario in the retest checklist): the mobile zip-in-chat composer upload silently fails on the Expo web preview — attaching a .zip via attach-doc-btn does NOT trigger the 'Indexing ZIP' alert, does NOT add a source to the chat, and the chip stays at 3 ZIPs. Root cause: /app/mobile/app/chat/[id].tsx pickDocument drops the DocumentPicker asset's `.file` Blob property when re-assembling the object it passes to uploadAsset, so uploadZipChunked falls out of its `Platform.OS === 'web' && asset.file` branch and into the native FileSystem.readAsStringAsync branch, which cannot read a blob: URI on web. The /documents screen doesn't have this bug because it forwards `asset as any` (with `.file` intact) directly.

ui_bugs.issue: Attaching a .zip via attach-doc-btn silently fails on Expo web preview. No 'Indexing ZIP' alert, no new chat-linked knowledge source is created, chip does not transition. Root cause: pickDocument in /app/mobile/app/chat/[id].tsx line 446-453 rebuilds the asset as {uri, name, type, size}, dropping the `.file` Blob property that DocumentPicker returns on web. uploadZipChunked at /app/mobile/src/chunkedUpload.ts:27 requires `asset.file` on web to take the uploadWebBlob path; otherwise it falls to the native FileSystem.readAsStringAsync branch which fails on blob: URIs. Fix: pass the asset through unchanged (as /documents does with `asset as any` at /app/mobile/app/documents/index.tsx:74) or explicitly forward `file: a.file` so both native and web work.

critical_code_review_comments: The two zip-upload entry points (Documents screen vs. Chat composer) share uploadZipChunked but pass the DocumentPicker asset differently — this divergence is exactly what caused the chat-zip bug. Consider centralising the asset-normalisation for uploadZipChunked so callers cannot accidentally strip `.file`.

chat/[id].tsx pickDocument silently swallows uploadAsset failures inside the for-loop (uploadAsset itself has a try/catch that only surfaces on non-.zip paths). A zip-upload failure surfaces no toast, no alert, no console error — the user has no signal that indexing didn't start. Add an error path (Alert.alert) around the .zip branch too, and/or log the failure in dev.
chat/[id].tsx is 1717 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Splitting the composer/upload/knowledge sub-features into modules would help avoid future divergence bugs like the .file drop above.

rca of the issue: Zip-in-chat upload silent failure — RCA: expo-document-picker's `getDocumentAsync` returns assets with a `.file` (Blob) property on web (necessary because blob: URIs cannot be read by expo-file-system.readAsStringAsync on web). /app/mobile/app/chat/[id].tsx:446 explicitly reconstructs the asset as `{uri: a.uri, name: a.name || 'file', type: a.mimeType || 'application/octet-stream', size: a.size}` — omitting `.file`. That trimmed object is passed to uploadAsset -> uploadZipChunked. In uploadZipChunked (line 27), the web branch requires `Platform.OS === 'web' && asset.file`; with `.file` missing, execution falls to the native branch which invokes `FileSystem.readAsStringAsync(asset.uri, {encoding: Base64})`. On Expo web, `asset.uri` is a `blob:` URL that expo-file-system/legacy cannot read, so the promise rejects. The rejection is caught in uploadAsset's try/catch (line 431-433) which shows 'Upload failed' Alert — but the caller (pickDocument's for-loop) awaits sequentially and the Alert only surfaces via React Native's web Alert modal (not the browser dialog handler used in the test). In practice we observed zero backend calls to /api/uploads/chunked/init from the chat composer path — confirming the client-side pre-check failed before any network I/O. Reproduction: (1) log in on mobile Expo preview, (2) open chat/d77a7d2a, (3) note chip shows 'AI knows 3 ZIPs', (4) tap attach-doc-btn, pick /tmp/test_facts.zip, (5) observe: no 'Indexing ZIP' alert, no new source in GET /api/knowledge/sources?chat_id=d77a7d2a, chip remains at 3 ZIPs. Mitigation: in chat/[id].tsx pickDocument, either forward the asset unchanged (`await uploadAsset(a as any)`) or explicitly copy `.file`: `await uploadAsset({uri: a.uri, name: a.name || 'file', type: a.mimeType || 'application/octet-stream', size: a.size, file: (a as any).file})`.
